name: Juri
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: h) Otras prosodias, tonos bajos, oclusión glotal y laringalización: No es fácil saber si los actuales tonos del tikuna (sistema en el que hay variantes dialectales importantes) tienen correspondencia con tonos o con acento. La grafía de los autores del vocabulario señala con frecuencia –y en lugares variados- al menos un acento ¿o tono alto? en cada palabra o construcción, pero hay palabras sin diacríticos. Ocasionalmente se marca un acento grave (34) pinà “cerveza y grano de maíz”.
new_statements.translation: h) Other prosodies, low tones, glottal stop and laryngealization: It is not easy to know whether the present-day tones of Tikuna (a system with important dialectal variants) correspond to tones or to accent. The spelling of the authors of the vocabulary frequently marks – and in varying positions – at least one accent (or high tone?) in each word or construction, but there are words without diacritics. Occasionally a grave accent is marked, (34) pinà 'beer and grain of maize'.
new_statements.citation: Goulard, Jean-Pierre & María Emilia Montes Rodríguez. 2013. Los yurí/juri-tikuna en el complejo socio-lingüístico del Noroeste Amazónico. LIAMES 13: 7-65.
new_statements.locator: p. 19, §2.2 h 'Otras prosodias, tonos bajos, oclusión glotal y laringalización' (corroborated by Carvalho 2009: 260-261, which reads the acute marks of Martius's Yurí items as stress marks, and by Wallace 1853: 521, 'the accent shows where the stress is to be laid')
new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule is recoverable. Yurí is known only from three 19th-century naturalists' wordlists (Martius 1820, Spix 1820, Wallace c.1850; Natterer 1833 ms.). Wallace states that his accent marks show where stress is laid; Carvalho 2009 takes the acute marks in Martius's list as stress marks and notes that Tikuna cognates preserve the Yurí stressed (often final) syllable (wikú > ku, seyú > ʤuʔú); Goulard & Montes 2013 conclude that the marks fall in varying positions, that some words carry none, and that it cannot be decided whether they record stress or high tone (the sister language Tikuna is tonal). Position of word accent therefore variable/lexical in the record, and its nature (stress vs tone) undetermined.
new_statements.exceptions: Words with no diacritic at all; occasional grave accent (pinà); Carvalho 2009: 261 notes that the acute-marked (stressed) syllable is not the one preserved when the first syllable contains a nasal or h (items 9, 10, 15, 18, 24, 25).
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms (isolated words, some with possessive prefix tschu-/su-/tcho-) elicited c. 1820-1850 and written in German-, Portuguese- and English-based orthographies; no connected speech, no native-speaker or instrumental data; the analysts (2009, 2013) work from these written forms only.
new_statements.identity_note: Juri = Yurí/Jurí (juri1235), an extinct language of the Içá-Japurá interfluve attested only in wordlists collected 1819-1850 (Martius at Uarivaú on the Japurá; Spix at Fonte Boa from Juri Tocano-Tapuüja transplanted from the Rio Puré; Wallace from Juri migrants on the Rio Negro; Natterer 1833 ms.). Goulard & Montes 2013 treat the three transcriptions as possibly different Yurí dialects. The uncontacted Carabayo (cara1245, ISO cby) of the Rio Puré are argued by Seifart & Echeverri 2014 to speak a Tikuna-Yurí language, possibly a descendant of Yurí; the sister language is Ticuna (ticu1245), which is tonal.

sources.citation: Orphão de Carvalho, Fernando. 2009. On the genetic kinship of the languages Tikúna and Yurí. Revista Brasileira de Linguística Antropológica 1(2): 247-268.
sources.note: §4.3 (pp. 256-261) sets up 25 Tikuna-Yurí comparanda from Martius 1867. p. 260: 'In the entries numbered 13 and 22, it seems that the Tikúna forms correspond to the stressed syllables of the Yurí forms... the unstressed syllables were lost, giving the pattern: wikú > [ku]; seyú > ([ʤu] > [ʤuʔú])'. p. 261: 'Taking the acute marks (´) as stress marks, we see that the forms in which the process of weak syllable deletion does not hold are the forms in which a nasal and/or a glottal fricative occurs in the first syllable (9, 10, 15, 18, 24, 25).' p. 259: in a few items Martius's vowel+h/gh corresp…

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1867. Juri. In Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, II: Wörtersammlung Brasilianischer Sprachen, 268-272. Leipzig: Fleischer.
sources.note: Latin-Juri wordlist collating Martius's own words (Uarivaú, from the principal Miguel, 1820), Spix's (Fonte Boa, Juri Tocano-Tapuüja) and Wallace's (footnote p. 268). Words carry scattered acute marks (e.g. gerühó, pinä, jahü, taöbi). The only convention statement is in the Tupi preface pp. 29-30: the acute 'dient, den Vocal zu schärfen oder die Sylbe zu betonen' and also separates vowels that do not form a diphthong; no Juri-specific prosodic remark.

sources.citation: Spix, Johann Baptist von & Carl Friedrich Philipp von Martius. 1831. Reise in Brasilien... Dritter Theil. München.
sources.note: Ethnographic narrative of the Juris at Uarivaú and Manacarú (Japurá), pp. c. 1223 ff.; no Juri wordlist located in this scanned (the words were published in Martius 1867). The one remark on 'Betonung' (p. c. 1213) concerns the Coëruna/Passé, not Juri.

sources.citation: Seifart, Frank & Juan Alvaro Echeverri. 2014. Evidence for the identification of Carabayo... as belonging to the Tikuna-Yurí linguistic family. PLoS ONE 9(4): e94814.
sources.note: p. 4: the Yurí wordlists were collected 1819-1820 by Martius and Spix, c. 1850 by Wallace, and in 1833 by Natterer (ms., Basel); all published in Martius 1867 except Natterer's. Cites Yurí forms with Wallace's accents (owúye, noré, háto). Nothing on Yurí stress; the accent remark (p. 2) concerns the 1969 Carabayo list.

sources.citation: Wallace, Alfred R. 1853. A narrative of travels on the Amazon and Rio Negro, with an account of the native tribes... London: Reeve. Appendix: Vocabularies of Amazonian languages (fold-out table incl. Juri).
sources.note: p. 521 (preface to the vocabularies): 'The words are spelt with the vowels sounded as in Portuguese... A til, thus ~, over a letter denotes that it has a nasal sound; the accent shows where the stress is to be laid; and a letter placed above the line shows that it is to be very faintly sounded'. The Juri column of the fold-out is scanned (lines c. 23436-23475) but the accents are lost in scanned; Seifart & Echeverri 2014 cite Wallace's Juri forms as owúye 'son', noré 'warm', háto 'father'. p. 510 describes the Juris of the Solimões; Latham's remarks (pp. 525-529) treat only the pronominal pre…
